does: Toasts sesame seeds until they are fragrant, then grinds them in a ridged bowl to a rough, oily paste with some seeds left half whole, ready to coat vegetables or to thicken a dressing.
how: Toast the seeds in a dry pan, shaking them, until they smell nutty and begin to pop.
Tip them into the ridged bowl while they are still warm.
Grind them with a circular motion, pressing against the ridges, until they are half crushed and oily.
Stir in the other seasonings and use the paste right away, as its scent fades.

cues.text: A deep, nutty, warm scent rises from the bowl.
The mixture turns into a damp, oily paste with some seeds left whole.

mistakes.mistake: Grinding raw seeds, which gives a pale, flat taste.
Grinding too long, which turns the paste greasy and pasty.
mistakes.fix: Stop while the seeds are still half whole.

variant_of.differs: The seeds are ground only until half crushed, in a ridged bowl, so that the paste stays rough and oily instead of becoming fine powder.
